# Independent manual workflows

`Bump version` makes a source-only branch commit with one required choice:
`patch`, `minor`, or `major` (default `patch`). `Build` has no custom inputs;
select the desired ref using GitHub's built-in selector. Neither workflow tags
or dispatches the other. All checkouts use immutable `github.sha`.

## Version authority

Intake: `034076c9029e73498249c6c5d2e61b5c9d06cf84`, version **1.0.3**.
Rename-follow history starts with marketing-only Bump at
`3045e1bb2f9de68bf246499fcabdfea3351f4ea1`. The explicit header at
`44f233d89003a11226a428b1b45eda2a7eb8ff3b` superseded that with coordinated
MARKETING_VERSION/CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION and plist versions, but its body
updated only the selected marketing key.

This migration does not increment the version. It aligns six stale source
CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION tokens from 1.0.1 to 1.0.3 and the two stale 2.0.0
display tokens in the English localization actually copied by Xcode.
Development, Deployment, and Default exist at target and project levels.
Info.plist's short version is required; its absent build key stays absent.
Prebuilt destination metadata is not authority and is unchanged.

Source validation rejects duplicates (including quoted/inline assignments),
missing/invalid/drifting fields, unknown references, cycles and configuration
topology changes before writing anything. Known references, unrelated values,
encodings, individual line endings and file modes are preserved.

## Safety and native policy

Bump requires its committed executable pre-push guard before edits and after
the final remote read. Every validation rejects symlinks, missing/nonexecutable
hooks, a non-100755 HEAD entry, or different raw hook bytes. It creates one
nonempty source-only direct child with explicit Actions bot author/committer
and the literal Copilot App trailer. The actual Git advertisement must contain
exactly the selected old SHA and one literal new SHA/HEAD branch update.
Advances, rewinds, deletions and same-result races fail without retries.
Both `push.followTags=false` and `--no-follow-tags` suppress followed tags.

Build preserves the actual macOS-only topology: Default universal
arm64+x86_64, deployment override 10.13, Cocoa/IOKit, the prebuilt
`a/liborsserialport.a`, and `test/Plugins/Serial.bundle`. Both committed
Windows and Windows64 binaries, QuickLook, and other resources are retained.
There is no new Windows job, dependency build, runtime architecture filter,
default-only branch restriction, or 4D execution. Architecture checks require
exact arm64 and x86_64 tokens, allowing extra architectures as before.

Cleanup removes only generated leaves and native intermediates, prevalidating
symlinks before deleting anything. It never removes entire bundles or Default
siblings. Built XML/binary plist and copied/compiled English localization are
checked. Signing requires strict verification; notarization requires both
exit zero and JSON `Accepted`, followed by stapling.

Build has a constant repository-wide publication concurrency group with
cancellation disabled (not a FIFO guarantee). Explicit nonempty GH_TOKEN and
early API/Git availability checks precede native work; the final gate follows
signing/notarization/stapling. Selected HEAD, the entire index, hidden index
flags and raw nongenerated bytes are independently checked. Generated tracked
bytes are retained, never reset to pretend the checkout is clean. Only exact
generated files, database/WAL companions, hashed XCBuildData records and proven
Serial intermediates may differ at the final gate. Initial ignored outputs and
unexpected ignored source/configuration files fail.

Publication checks every release page through an empty page, including drafts,
the exact API tag ref and exact Git tag advertisement. All read failures,
malformed/duplicate/nonfinite JSON and same-SHA tag races fail closed.
Separate create-only POSTs create the tag at selected SHA, a new public release
ID and its two assets, `Serial-X.Y.Z.zip` and `Serial-X.Y.Z.dmg`. The original
empty release body/no generated notes policy is preserved. No existing release,
tag or asset is reused, updated, clobbered or deleted. Intake already has a
v1.0.3 release, so Build on unchanged intake intentionally refuses publication.
Run Bump separately before releasing a new version.

**Manual recovery:** a failed POST or lost response may leave partial state.
Inspect the reported tag, release ID and retained uploads manually before
another Build. No rollback, deletion, retry or automatic repair is performed.

## Offline validation

Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`
(PyYAML required), then `actionlint` across both workflows.
Tests use local bare Git, fake GitHub APIs and closed-PATH native/credential
doubles; they never execute real compilers, signing, notarization or 4D.
Intake fixtures are immutable; live expectations also pass after a genuine
guarded source-only Bump. Hash-verified reference provenance is recorded in
`tests/reference-pins.json`.
